newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian activist says government tried to kill him.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian activist says government tried to kill him.

text.p: A leading member of a Nigerian opposition group accused the military government of sending gunmen on Tuesday to kill him after they riddled his car with bullets.
"Who else can I suspect other than the Nigerian military government?" asked Senator Abraham Adesanya at a news conference in his office in Lagos.
"The government doesn't want me to live. They hate me because I criticise their politics and policies. But they will not succeed because I haven't offended anybody," he added.
Earlier, the 74-year-old lawyer told Reuters unidentified gunmen fired several bullets at his car on a Lagos street on his way to court in an attempt on his life.
Adesanya said he had reported the matter to the police who had inspected his bullet-riddled Mercedes car "The police said they will investigate the matter," he added.
Scores of sympathisers for Adesanya and the opposition NADECO group were at the news conference.

"I'm shocked at this cowardly attack on both Adesanya and NADECO. It also confirms his earlier suspicions that there were plans to kill him and other NADECO members," said Kofo Bucknor-Akerele, a NADECO woman activist.
Last week Adesanya alleged at a news conference in Lagos that he and Michael Ajasin, the octogenarian leader of NADECO, were marked out for elimination.

NADECO (National Democratic Coalition) is the umbrella organisation of pro-democracy groups that back Moshood Abiola, the presumed winner of a 1993 presidential poll which was annulled by a previous army government.
Abiola has been detained since 1994 when he proclaimed himself president in defiance of the military authorities.

Three unexplained bomb attacks since December have killed at least three soldiers and wounded dozens of people in Lagos. The government blames the exiled opposition, which it says is linked to NADECO, for the bombings.
Adesanya is one of three elderly opposition politicians the police detained last year over the murder by unknown gunmen of Abiola's senior wife in Lagos.
The three were freed on court orders but told to report to the police at weekly intervals.
Adesanya said he doubted the police would find those who he said had tried to kill him.
Apart from Abiola's wife, several other prominent Nigerians have either been killed or suffered assassination attempts in the last year in mysterious circumstances.
None of the murders or attempted murders have been solved by police.
